curated_notes: PK values are reported only for DualAG, and only in a single RESULTS sentence: Tmax 5 h and T1/2 1.7 h after 3 mg/kg s.c. in lean C57Bl/6 mice. Sequences were not extracted because the PEPLIFE2 header is database metadata and the body does not print the amino-acid sequences. Roles: dextrose is a metabolic challenge agent rather than a test article; the protocol role enum does not cover this, so 'other' is used. Anaesthetics (isofluorane) are procedural and are not listed as agents.

curated_notes: IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON THE HALF-LIFE. The only half-life in the body, 3.6 h, comes from incubating the peptide in serum harvested from a CPC;Apc mouse at 37 °C and following it by RP-HPLC over 24 h. It is a proteolytic stability half-life measured ex vivo, not a plasma elimination half-life from a dosed animal, so half_life_phase is 'unspecified' and both half_life_absorption and half_life_elimination are 'not reported'. The paper's own section heading 'In Vivo Serum Stability' is misleading relative to its Methods; the matrix field records the assay as it was actually performed. No plasma or blood concentrations were ever measured in this study, so there is no Cmax, tmax or AUC. The in vivo pharmacokinetics section is entirely imaging-based: 'Quantified intensities showed a peak T/B ratio at 1 h after injection of QQT*-IRDye800. The signal decreased to the baseline by ~24 h post-injection', and Figure 5a gives 'a mean (±SD) value of 2.2 ± 0.4 at 1 h post-injection with clearance by ~24 h'. That 1 h peak is a tumour-to-background fluorescence ratio maximum, not a plasma tmax, so it was deliberately not entered in the tmax field. Dose is reported only as a concentration and volume (200 μM, 200 μL); no body weight normalised dose is given. Human involvement was limited to donor-derived colonoid tissue (adenoma from a 46-year-old male and a 64-year-old male, normal colon from a 43-year-old female deceased donor) cultured in vitro; no human subject was dosed, so clinical_detail is null. Biodistribution at 1 h showed strong kidney signal consistent with renal clearance, with increased liver and lung intensity attributed to vasculature; no toxicity was seen on necropsy, hematology or chemistry at 48 h.

curated_notes: UNITS TRAP RESOLVED: Table 1's parameter column is printed as 't1/2h'. It is a half-life expressed in hours, not a rate constant in h-1. Evidence used: the parameter name is t1/2, and the body text states 'The average half-lives were approximately 20-25 min in mice, 30 min in rats and 40 min in dogs' and 'In monkeys, the average half-life was approximately 55 min', which match the tabulated 0.306-0.547 h (mouse), 0.248-0.805 h (rat), 0.615-0.668 h (dog) and 0.888-0.956 h (monkey). No ln(2)/k conversion was performed by the curator. RATE CONSTANT HANDLED SEPARATELY: human Table 2 lists lambda_last of 0.3607, 0.4082 and 0.4338 1/h; these were recorded verbatim in pk_quote and were NOT converted into half-lives, because the same table already reports the fitted t1/2 values. Cmax vs C0: Table 1 reports C0 (concentration back-extrapolated to time zero) for the animal species, not an observed Cmax; the Results text nonetheless describes 'systemic exposure of CEND-1, expressed as Cmax and AUClast' and the Discussion says 'this dose results in a Cmax (C0) of approximately 40 microg/mL'. Both the label and the value are recorded so the distinction is not lost. No tmax is reported for any animal species (intravenous dosing); tmax IS reported for humans (0.063-0.117 h). No absorption half-life is reported for any species, as all dosing was intravenous. DOSE INCONSISTENCY INSIDE THE BODY: Methods 4.1 states '1, 5 and 50 mg/kg for rats, dogs and monkeys', but Table 1 lists 1, 5 and 75 mg/kg for rats and dogs; both are recorded. Study-type scope: this article covers mouse, rat, dog, cynomolgus monkey and human; the mouse PK values (t1/2 0.306/0.344/0.547 h) are the ones matching the PEPLIFE2 header rows. Curation rule applied: procedural probe, contrast and anaesthetic substances are documented here rather than listed as agents - Evans blue (33.3 mg/kg i.v., extracted from tissue in N,N-dimethylformamide and quantified at 600 nm), Gd-DTPA, Gd-DOTA and gadoxetic acid (Gd-EOB-DTPA) MRI contrast agents, and ketamine (70 mg/kg) plus xylazine (10 mg/kg) and isoflurane as anaesthetics. nab-paclitaxel and gemcitabine are co-administered background chemotherapy rather than true comparator arms; they are given role 'comparator' only because the schema role enum has no 'co-administered therapy' option. Excision and extraction of tissues for QRA and Evans blue quantification were treated as bioanalysis of in vivo samples, not as a separate ex vivo experiment, consistent with the handling of plasma assays.

RATE CONSTANT HANDLED SEPARATELY: human Table 2 lists lambda_last of 0.3607, 0.4082 and 0.4338 1/h; these were recorded verbatim in pk_quote and were NOT converted into half-lives, because the same table already reports the fitted t1/2 values. curated_half_lives: Onc72: 43 min (elimination t1/2, Table 1; text states "an elimination half-life of ~43 min") [CD-1 mouse plasma (K2EDTA) after subcutaneous administration] ;; 5k-prodrug (5 kDa PEG-Leu-Val-Pro-Arg-Onc72): 66 min (elimination t1/2 in mouse plasma, cELISA total Onc72); 8 h for Onc72 release in mouse serum ex vivo [CD-1 mouse plasma (in vivo elimination); mouse serum (ex vivo release half-life)] ;; 20k-prodrug (20 kDa PEG-Leu-Val-Pro-Arg-Onc72): 324 min (Table 1); text reports "prolonged elimination t1/2 of 66 min and even 5.5 h"; 14 h for Onc72 release in mouse serum ex vivo [CD-1 mouse plasma (in vivo elimination); mouse serum (ex vivo release half-life)]
curated_doses: Onc72: single dose of 4.34 µmol kg-1 body weight (corresponding to 10 mg kg-1 Onc72) subcutaneous (SC) ;; 5k-prodrug (5 kDa PEG-Leu-Val-Pro-Arg-Onc72): single dose of 4.34 µmol kg-1 body weight subcutaneous (SC) ;; 20k-prodrug (20 kDa PEG-Leu-Val-Pro-Arg-Onc72): single dose of 4.34 µmol kg-1 body weight subcutaneous (SC) ;; 5 kDa thiol-PEG: 50 µmol L-1 final concentration in vitro not applicable - in vitro incubation only (not administered to animals) ;; 20 kDa thiol-PEG: 50 µmol L-1 final concentration in vitro not applicable - in vitro incubation only (not administered to animals) ;; Triton X-100: serial dilution from 0.1% to 0.00078% not applicable - ex vivo human erythrocyte hemolysis assay ;; DMSO: 12% (v/v) in medium not applicable - cell culture positive control ;; Phosphate-buffered saline (PBS): PBS 12% (v/v) in medium (cytotoxicity); undiluted PBS in hemolysis assay not applicable - in vitro/ex vivo negative control ;; 13C,15N-labeled Onc72 (and labeled 1-11Onc72): 62.5 or 125 fmol µL-1 spiked into plasma/urine aliquots not applicable - analytical internal standard
curated_bioanalytical_method: Competitive ELISA (cELISA) using protein-G-captured anti-Onc72 monoclonal antibody 4H6 with carboxyfluorescein-Onc72 reporter (fluorescence, lambda-exc 485 nm / lambda-em 535 nm) for total Onc72; plus LC-MS (ACQUITY UPLC M-Class coupled to ESI-QTOF Synapt G2-Si, scheduled multiple reaction monitoring) with 13C,15N-labeled Onc72 internal standard for free Onc72 and metabolites; RP-HPLC/ESI-IT-MS for serum and lysate release experiments; HDMSE for urine metabolite identification
curated_notes: Elimination half-lives are for total Onc72-immunoreactive material (prodrug + released Onc72 + epitope-containing metabolites) measured by cELISA; Table 1 gives t1/2 43, 66 and 324 min for Onc72, 5k-prodrug and 20k-prodrug respectively, while the body text describes the 20k-prodrug value as '~5.5 h'. The ex vivo mouse-serum release half-lives (8 h for 5k-prodrug, 14 h for 20k-prodrug) come from Figure 1 and are release, not elimination, half-lives. Additional Table 1 parameters: V 47.3 / 115.3 / 171.8 mL, AUC0-inf 5.5 / 12.7 / 139 µg x h/mL, CL 0.76 / 1.22 / 0.35 mL min-1, MRT 53 / 111 / 524 min. The body states Onc72 has a reported mouse-serum half-life of ~3 h and an intraperitoneal elimination t1/2 of ~14 min, but both are explicitly attributed to earlier publications and were therefore not extracted. Mice were grouped by blood-sampling timepoint (groups 1-3) rather than by a fixed n per arm. LOD/LOQ: 4.5 and 9 µg L-1 for Onc72; cELISA urine LOQ 46 µg L-1. Lower-detail agents also present in the body but not separately listed: human alpha-thrombin (enzymatic release reagent), Cf-Onc72 reporter, mAb 4H6, recombinant protein G, casein.

The file header shows 'PMID: ?' with PMC9164557; the PMID was supplied by the assignment.

curated_notes: PK was measured by whole-plasma DOX fluorescence on an IVIS imager rather than by a chromatographic assay, so the reported half-lives are fluorescence-decay half-lives of total DOX signal. The body never states the number of animals in the PK arm, nor group sizes for any in vivo arm, so group_n is 'not reported' throughout. The half-life for Al-ProD is given only as an inequality ('more than 3 h') and no phase is named anywhere in the body, hence half_life_phase 'unspecified' and both phase-specific fields 'not reported'; the authors fitted no compartmental model and reported no rate constants. AUC evidence quote (verbatim, RESULTS): 'the area under the curve (AUC) of Al-ProD was approximately sevenfold increased compared with that of free DOX' - no units or absolute values are given. Additional in vivo timing detail: 'a detectable amount of the Al-ProD remained for 144 h in the body'. Note the paper uses the phrase 'ex vivo imaging' for fluorescence imaging of organs resected from dosed mice at 12 h; that is a readout of in vivo biodistribution rather than an ex vivo treatment of isolated tissue, so 'ex vivo' was not added to study_types. Albumin (HSA, MSA, BSA), recombinant cathepsins/caspases and cathepsin B-inhibitory siRNA were incubation partners or tools rather than administered/tested therapeutic substances and were not given agent objects. In vitro potency for reference: IC50 of HSA-bound Al-ProD was 7.33 uM in MDA-MB231 versus >200 uM in H9C2.

curated_notes: IMPORTANT INTERPRETIVE CAVEAT stated by the authors: these are total-14C 'pseudo-pharmacokinetic' parameters, not parameters for intact WLBU2. The DISCUSSION states 'The pseudo-pharmacokinetic parameters of 14C content are a composite of the underlying individual parameters of the respective analytes with the 14C label. The 22 h terminal half-life of plasma radioactivity is, therefore, likely not the true terminal half-life, which would only be revealed with much longer sampling.' Roughly 34% of the dose was unaccounted for at 24 h and is attributed to expiration of 14CO2 after cleavage to the 14C-valine label. Parameters were derived by non-compartmental analysis from average concentration values using PK Solutions 2.0; only a terminal/elimination half-life is reported, and no absorption phase or absorption half-life is described (dosing was intravenous). Unit-header inconsistency in Table 2: the Cmax and AUC0-24 row labels carry per-gram units while the plasma column is per-mL; the parameter names and body text were used to assign plasma Cmax = 47.0±16.7 ug-eq/mL and plasma AUC0-24 = 266.6 ug-eq*h/g as printed. There is also an internal inconsistency on the single-dose MTD: the ABSTRACT says 20 mg/kg while the RESULTS body says 'The IV single dose MTD for WLBU2 is 30 mg/kg' and the DISCUSSION says 'The murine IV single dose, and daily x 5 MTD for WLBU2 were 30 and 15 mg/kg, respectively'; the body values are used here. Control plasma and control lung/liver/kidney homogenates were spiked with [14C]-WLBU2 or WLBU2 as bioanalytical recovery controls; these are method-validation steps rather than a biological ex vivo assay, so no ex vivo study type is claimed. An untreated (no injection) control group was included in the multiple-dose MTD study; it receives no substance and is therefore not listed as an agent.

curated_bioanalytical_method: Sandwich ELISA for total mouse OCN (goat polyclonal anti-MID OCN capture, goat polyclonal anti-CTERM OCN detection) for mouse samples; commercial human ucOCN ELISA (BioLegend 446707, 8H4 capture / 4B6 detection) for human protein. Full amino-acid sequences appear only in figure graphics (Fig. 1E, Fig. 5A) and are not printed in the body text.

The PeplLife2 metadata labels the row 'In Vitro' and gives the assay as 'N.A.'; the actual assay described in the body is radio-TLC with liquid scintillation counting, not a chromatographic UV method. The PeplLife2 half-life of 5.6 +/- 0.2 min in mouse blood matches the body exactly. NOTE an internal inconsistency in the source: the Results section gives the human whole-blood half-life as 5.2 +/- 0.4 min, whereas the Discussion states 'a half-life of less than 4 min' for human whole blood; both figures are in the body and neither has been altered here. The ~12 min half-life in human plasma is cited from earlier work (Bramucci et al.), not measured here. There is also an apparent arithmetic inconsistency in the Methods between the stated 30 ng of labelled peptide added to 1 mL of blood and the stated final concentration of 93 nmol/mL; both values are quoted verbatim without correction. Rate constants for the rat/mouse model are given in the Fig. 6 caption (k1 = 0.15, k2 = 0.02, k3 = 0.08, k4 = 0.05, k5 = 0.025, k6 = 0.25, k7 = 0.03, k8 = 0.2, k9 = 0.0, k10 = 0.01 min^-1; A0 = 88.0). Mouse blood produced only two major fragments (2-8 and 2-6) versus three (2-8, 3-8, 2-6) in rat and human blood, and the authors conclude 'mouse would appear to be a less satisfactory model for the proteolysis in blood than the rat'.

Methods state the mouse PK study had '4 groups, 3 doses ... and 2 dose routes ... with 18 animals in each group' for 72 mice, which is internally inconsistent (3 x 2 = 6 arms); recorded verbatim.

curated_notes: IMPORTANT: the half-life value of '< 30 min' carried in the PeplLife2 metadata appears ONLY in the abstract. No half-life, t1/2 or elimination-rate value is stated anywhere after '=== BODY ==='; the body reports only concentrations at discrete time points and an AUC. half_life is therefore recorded as 'not reported in body'. The body's only elimination statement is qualitative: 'Api137 is very rapidly eliminated from the blood stream'. AUC values reported in the body (Fig. 6 caption and Discussion) are 89 ug*min/mL for continuous sc infusion at 19.2 mg/kg/h over 6-20 h post implantation, versus predicted 92 (iv) and 7 (sc) ug*min/mL for 10 mg/kg every 30 min. The ED50 for 50% survival by continuous sc infusion was 13.4 mg/kg/h. Two separate pump experiments exist: an initial series primed for 3 h at doses of 9.6, 12.8 and 16 mg/kg/h that gave inconsistent, non-dose-dependent plasma levels, and an optimized series primed for 6 h at 6.4, 12.8 and 19.2 mg/kg/h that gave the stable levels reported above. Tolerance findings: 50 mg/kg iv was lethal in mice within 1 min. Prior-publication PK values quoted in the Introduction for comparison (Onc72 and Onc112 at 1.8/5.4 mg/L ip and 5.7/8.4 mg/L iv; Api88 and Api137 at 1.0/0.4 mg/L iv and 0.6/0.2 mg/L ip after 5 mg/kg) are cited from earlier work, not measured here. curated_notes: IMPORTANT SPECIES CAVEAT: all pharmacokinetic work in this paper was done in RATS (female Wistar, n = 4 per group), not mice. The body does state mouse half-life values for lysostaphin, Cpl-1 and LytA, but only in the Introduction as citations of prior literature, not as data generated here: 'The estimated serum half-life of anti-staphylococcal lysin lysostaphin in mice was less than 1 h, and the half-life times of anti-pneumococcal lysins Cpl-1 and LytA were measured to be 20.5 and 22.5 min, respectively.' Cpl-1 and LytA were never produced, administered or assayed in this study and are therefore not listed as agents. Reported PK: lysostaphin terminal t1/2 1.5 ± 0.7 h and AUC 3.5 ± 2.4 mg·h/L; Lst-HDD terminal t1/2 3.1 ± 0.6 h and AUC 9.1 ± 2.8 mg·h/L. No Cmax or Tmax was determined; the first sample was at 25 min, where concentrations were 2.8 ± 0.2 µg/mL (lysostaphin) and 1.6 ± 0.1 µg/mL (Lst-HDD) against a theoretical post-injection concentration of ~50 µg/mL, indicating ~95% had already been eliminated. Amino-acid sequences appear only as a figure graphic (Fig. 1B) and are not extractable from the body text.

The body explicitly explains the choice: 'Because albumin has a half-life of 1.9 days in rats and 1.0 day in mice, we selected old female Sprague-Dawley rats... for the single-dose pharmacokinetic study.' The mouse experiment in the PK section was a qualitative Western blot of albumin conjugation, with no PK parameters. There is a dose discrepancy for F56-CM in mice: Methods give '5 mg/mL in PBS, injection volume, 10 mL/kg' while the Fig. 4A caption gives '5 mg/kg'; both are recorded verbatim and no arithmetic conversion was performed. Biodistribution %IA/g values at 4 h and 8 h in tumour-bearing nude mice are reported (Fig. 4E-F) but are not Cmax/AUC parameters and are not entered in the PK fields. curated_notes: Cmax and tmax are not reported for either probe; dosing was intravenous, so no absorption phase exists and no absorption half-life is reported. The PEPLIFE2 header lists the F1A peptide sequence as QWECPYGLCWIQ; the article body prints QIWCLGYPCEWQ and the body was used. Procedural agents administered but not tested as study articles are recorded here rather than as agent objects: ketamine (85 mg/kg)/xylazine (10 mg/kg) plus 1-2% isoflurane for anaesthesia, and Rose Bengal dye (60 ug/g body weight by tail vein, 20 mg/mL) with HeNe laser photoactivation to create the carotid thrombus model. Unlabeled (cold) F1A and excess cysteine were used only as in vitro competitors. Human LVADs came from patients but no patient was dosed, so the study is not classified as clinical.

curated_notes: The supplied full-text file contains no METHODS or Experimental Section, so the bioanalytical assay, the exact PK dose and the PK sampling schedule are not recoverable from the body. The PEPLIFE2 header lists the assay as LC-MS/SIM; that is database metadata and was not used, so bioanalytical_method is recorded as not reported. The only PK datum in the body is the approximately 6 h plasma half-life of peptide 21 after intraperitoneal dosing. No phase is named, so half_life_phase is 'unspecified' and half_life_elimination is left as not reported rather than inferred. Dosing was intraperitoneal, so an absorption phase exists, but no absorption half-life and no rate constant is reported and nothing was converted. No Cmax, tmax or AUC is reported. The dose used specifically for the PK study is not stated; 20 mg/kg ip is the dose given for the HDL remodeling experiment in the immediately preceding sentence and 7.5 mg/kg ip was used for the anti-inflammatory study, so the PK dose is recorded as not separately stated. The eight-hour persistence of the pre-beta HDL effect is a pharmacodynamic duration, not a half-life. Over 80 cyclic d,l-alpha-peptides were screened (81 sequences per the Results text, with 73 eight-residue and 8 six-residue peptides); only the sequences printed in the body text or in Table 1 are captured as agent objects, and the remainder are listed only in Table S1, which is not part of the supplied body. Peptides 1, 15, 18, 23-26, 33, 34, 36-39, 41-50 and 52-54 are discussed by number in the Results without their sequences being printed. Lipopolysaccharide (LPS), given intraperitoneally to induce the acute inflammation model, is a model-induction agent and is noted here rather than listed as an agent object.

curated_notes: Priority fields: Tmax is reported for both matrices (stomach 10 min, intestine 40 min) and both are described by the authors as an "absorption peak time". No Cmax, no AUC and no absorption half-life are reported - the assay yields relative exposure (peak intensity ratio), so absolute concentrations were deliberately not determined by iMScope. The half-lives are tissue elimination half-lives from stomach and intestine, NOT plasma half-lives; the body explicitly says "according the elimination rate of octreotide in mouse intestine" and the Section 3.5 heading names elimination for the stomach. Both stomach values are consistent between the Introduction summary ("28.0 min") and Results ("28 min"). The intestinal value was independently reproduced by LC-MS/MS (35.6 min), which the authors report as not significantly different. Half-lives were computed with Phoenix WinNonlin. Doses were given by gavage, so the apparent tissue elimination reflects both absorption from the lumen and clearance from the tissue - the paper does not separate these. The MALDI matrices (DHB, CHCA, SA) and the gelatin used to fill the gastrointestinal cavity post mortem were not recorded as agents because they are sample-preparation reagents, not administered or tested articles. The PEPLIFE2 header rows (28 min stomach, 37.7 min intestine) match the body and were used only to know which peptide to look for.

curated_notes: Abstract was fenced and was not used. Table 2 was legible and the two data columns were confirmed as HSA-dTMP then dTMP-HSA because the t1/2 row (17.1, 16.1) matches the Results prose exactly. Full Table 2 values: t1/2 17.1 vs 16.1 h; CL1/F 4559 vs 4387 l/h/kg; AUC(0-inf) 25,699 vs 35,018 h*ng/ml; V1/F 106,186 vs 102,078 l/kg; Tmax 2.32 vs 2.39 h. NOTE that the reported clearance and volume of distribution are physically implausible for a mouse (thousands of l/h/kg, hundred thousand l/kg) and almost certainly carry a unit or scaling error in the source; they are recorded verbatim as printed and are not used to derive anything. NO Cmax is reported - Table 2 lists only t1/2, CL1/F, AUC(0-inf), V1/F and Tmax, and the Results prose adds nothing further, so cmax is "not reported" for both fusion proteins even though tmax is given. NO absorption half-life and no absorption rate constant (Ka) are reported, despite an extravascular one-compartment fit that would normally yield one; nothing was converted or inferred. half_life_phase is "unspecified" because the paper defines the parameter only as "t1/2, half-life in serum" and never names an elimination, distribution or terminal phase. The Results text says "in plasma" in one sentence while the Methods, Table 2 footnote and Fig. 8 caption all say serum; serum is recorded as the matrix. The statement in the Discussion that the fusion half-life is "about 15-fold higher than that of dTMP" rests on a literature value for dTMP (approximately 1 h, cited to de Serres et al. 1999 in the Introduction); dTMP itself was NOT dosed in this study, so no half-life is recorded for it and it is not listed as an agent. The Ethical approval statement mentions procedures on "mice and rabbits", and an anti-TMP rabbit polyclonal antibody was prepared in-house, but no rabbit experiment is described in the body, so rabbit is not listed as a dosed species. The signal peptide MKWVTFISLLFLFSSAYSRGVFRR is explicitly identified in the body as HSA's natural secretion signal and is therefore cleaved from the mature secreted protein; it is reported here as part of the expressed precursor only.

NO Cmax, tmax or AUC is reported anywhere in the body. The plasma ELISA readout is explicitly normalised ("The absorbance of the sample collected at 1 min was considered to be 100%"), so the study never produced absolute plasma concentrations and no Cmax could exist. NO absorption half-life and no rate constant are reported; the authors give only a single "circulating half-life" with no named phase, so half_life_phase is "unspecified" and half_life_elimination is left "not reported" rather than inferred. The BB28 value is a censored upper bound ("less than 5 min") and is recorded verbatim as such. Peptides used in the PK study were N-terminally biotinylated so that they could be captured by streptavidin-HRP; this label is noted in the sequence fields. Terminal fluorescence scanning of excised organs at 24 h is a biodistribution readout on tissue from dosed animals rather than an ex vivo incubation, so "ex vivo" was not added as a study type even though the figure legend uses that word. B28 (GGLRSLGRKILRAWKKYG) and the ABD heptapeptide WQRPSSW are named in the body as building blocks but were not themselves dosed or assayed as standalone agents, so they are not listed as separate agent objects. Cytotoxicity IC50 values (micromolar) are rendered in this PDF text with "mM" where "uM" is meant, an extraction artefact of the mu character; the IC50 numbers are not PK parameters and were not used for any PK field.
